verses.ar: فَتَفَرَّسَ بُولُسُ فِي ٱلْمَجْمَعِ وَقَالَ: «أَيُّهَا ٱلرِّجَالُ ٱلْإِخْوَةُ، إِنِّي بِكُلِّ ضَمِيرٍ صَالِحٍ قَدْ عِشْتُ لِلهِ إِلَى هَذَا ٱلْيَوْمِ».
verses.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men [and] brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.web: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”

verses.ar: فَأَمَرَ حَنَانِيَّا رَئِيسُ ٱلْكَهَنَةِ، ٱلْوَاقِفِينَ عِنْدَهُ أَنْ يَضْرِبُوهُ عَلَى فَمِهِ.
verses.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.web: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

verses.ar: حِينَئِذٍ قَالَ لَهُ بُولُسُ: «سَيَضْرِبُكَ ٱللهُ أَيُّهَا ٱلْحَائِطُ ٱلْمُبَيَّضُ! أَفَأَنْتَ جَالِسٌ تَحْكُمُ عَلَيَّ حَسَبَ ٱلنَّامُوسِ، وَأَنْتَ تَأْمُرُ بِضَرْبِي مُخَالِفًا لِلنَّامُوسِ؟».
verses.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, [thou] whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.web: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”

verses.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلْوَاقِفُونَ: «أَتَشْتِمُ رَئِيسَ كَهَنَةِ ٱللهِ؟»
verses.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
verses.web: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”

verses.ar: فَقَالَ بُولُسُ: «لَمْ أَكُنْ أَعْرِفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلْإِخْوَةُ أَنَّهُ رَئِيسُ كَهَنَةٍ، لِأَنَّهُ مَكْتُوبٌ: رَئِيسُ شَعْبِكَ لَا تَقُلْ فِيهِ سُوءًا».
verses.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
verses.web: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”

verses.ar: وَلَمَّا عَلِمَ بُولُسُ أَنَّ قِسْمًا مِنْهُمْ صَدُّوقِيُّونَ وَٱلْآخَرَ فَرِّيسِيُّونَ، صَرَخَ فِي ٱلْمَجْمَعِ: «أَيُّهَا ٱلرِّجَالُ ٱلْإِخْوَةُ، أَنَا فَرِّيسِيٌّ ٱبْنُ فَرِّيسِيٍّ. عَلَى رَجَاءِ قِيَامَةِ ٱلْأَمْوَاتِ أَنَا أُحَاكَمُ».
verses.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men [and] brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.web: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”

verses.ar: وَلَمَّا قَالَ هَذَا حَدَثَتْ مُنَازَعَةٌ بَيْنَ ٱلْفَرِّيسِيِّينَ وَٱلصَّدُّوقِيِّينَ، وَٱنْشَقَّتِ ٱلْجَمَاعَةُ،
verses.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.web: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.

verses.ar: لِأَنَّ ٱلصَّدُّوقِيِّينَ يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ قِيَامَةٌ وَلَا مَلَاكٌ وَلَا رُوحٌ، وَأَمَّا ٱلْفَرِّيسِيُّونَ فَيُقِرُّونَ بِكُلِّ ذَلِكَ.
verses.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.web: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

verses.ar: فَحَدَثَ صِيَاحٌ عَظِيمٌ، وَنَهَضَ كَتَبَةُ قِسْمِ ٱلْفَرِّيسِيِّينَ وَطَفِقُوا يُخَاصِمُونَ قَائِلِينَ: «لَسْنَا نَجِدُ شَيْئًا رَدِيًّا فِي هَذَا ٱلْإِنْسَانِ! وَإِنْ كَانَ رُوحٌ أَوْ مَلَاكٌ قَدْ كَلَّمَهُ فَلَا نُحَارِبَنَّ ٱللهَ».
verses.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes [that were] of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
verses.web: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”

verses.ar: وَلَمَّا حَدَثَتْ مُنَازَعَةٌ كَثِيرَةٌ ٱخْتَشَى ٱلْأَمِيرُ أَنْ يَفْسَخُوا بُولُسَ، فَأَمَرَ ٱلْعَسْكَرَ أَنْ يَنْزِلُوا وَيَخْتَطِفُوهُ مِنْ وَسْطِهِمْ وَيَأْتُوا بِهِ إِلَى ٱلْمُعَسْكَرِ.
verses.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring [him] into the castle.
verses.web: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.

verses.ar: وَفِي ٱللَّيْلَةِ ٱلتَّالِيَةِ وَقَفَ بِهِ ٱلرَّبُّ وَقَالَ: «ثِقْ يَا بُولُسُ! لِأَنَّكَ كَمَا شَهِدْتَ بِمَا لِي فِي أُورُشَلِيمَ، هَكَذَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَشْهَدَ فِي رُومِيَةَ أَيْضًا».
verses.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.web: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

verses.ar: وَلَمَّا صَارَ ٱلنَّهَارُ صَنَعَ بَعْضُ ٱلْيَهُودِ ٱتِّفَاقًا، وَحَرَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ قَائِلِينَ: إِنَّهُمْ لَا يَأْكُلُونَ وَلَا يَشْرَبُونَ حَتَّى يَقْتُلُوا بُولُسَ.
verses.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
verses.web: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.ar: وَكَانَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَنَعُوا هَذَا ٱلتَّحَالُفَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ.
verses.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.web: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

verses.ar: فَتَقَدَّمُوا إِلَى رُؤَسَاءِ ٱلْكَهَنَةِ وَٱلشُّيُوخِ وَقَالُوا: «قَدْ حَرَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا حِرْمًا أَنْ لَا نَذُوقَ شَيْئًا حَتَّى نَقْتُلَ بُولُسَ.
verses.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.web: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

verses.ar: وَٱلْآنَ أَعْلِمُوا ٱلْأَمِيرَ أَنْتُمْ مَعَ ٱلْمَجْمَعِ لِكَيْ يُنْزِلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ غَدًا، كَأَنَّكُمْ مُزْمِعُونَ أَنْ تَفْحَصُوا بِأَكْثَرِ تَدْقِيقٍ عَمَّا لَهُ. وَنَحْنُ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقْتَرِبَ، مُسْتَعِدُّونَ لِقَتْلِهِ».
verses.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.web: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”

verses.ar: وَلَكِنَّ ٱبْنَ أُخْتِ بُولُسَ سَمِعَ بِٱلْكَمِينِ، فَجَاءَ وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمُعَسْكَرَ وَأَخْبَرَ بُولُسَ.
verses.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.web: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

verses.ar: فَٱسْتَدْعَى بُولُسُ وَاحِدًا مِنْ قُوَّادِ ٱلْمِئَاتِ وَقَالَ: «ٱذْهَبْ بِهَذَا ٱلشَّابِّ إِلَى ٱلْأَمِيرِ، لِأَنَّ عِنْدَهُ شَيْئًا يُخْبِرُهُ بِهِ».
verses.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto [him], and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.web: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”

verses.ar: فَأَخَذَهُ وَأَحْضَرَهُ إِلَى ٱلْأَمِيرِ وَقَالَ: «ٱسْتَدْعَانِي ٱلْأَسِيرُ بُولُسُ، وَطَلَبَ أَنْ أُحْضِرَ هَذَا ٱلشَّابَّ إِلَيْكَ، وَهُوَ عِنْدَهُ شَيْءٌ لِيَقُولَهُ لَكَ».
verses.kjv: So he took him, and brought [him] to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto [him], and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.web: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

verses.ar: فَأَخَذَ ٱلْأَمِيرُ بِيَدِهِ وَتَنَحَّى بِهِ مُنْفَرِدًا، وَٱسْتَخْبَرَهُ: «مَا هُوَ ٱلَّذِي عِنْدَكَ لِتُخْبِرَنِي بِهِ؟».
verses.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went [with him] aside privately, and asked [him], What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.web: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”

verses.ar: فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ ٱلْيَهُودَ تَعَاهَدُوا أَنْ يَطْلُبُوا مِنْكَ أَنْ تُنْزِلَ بُولُسَ غَدًا إِلَى ٱلْمَجْمَعِ، كَأَنَّهُمْ مُزْمِعُونَ أَنْ يَسْتَخْبِرُوا عَنْهُ بِأَكْثَرِ تَدْقِيقٍ.
verses.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.web: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

verses.ar: فَلَا تَنْقَدْ إِلَيْهِمْ، لِأَنَّ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ رَجُلًا مِنْهُمْ كَامِنُونَ لَهُ، قَدْ حَرَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ أَنْ لَا يَأْكُلُوا وَلَا يَشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَقْتُلُوهُ. وَهُمُ ٱلْآنَ مُسْتَعِدُّونَ مُنْتَظِرُونَ ٱلْوَعْدَ مِنْكَ».
verses.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.web: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”

verses.ar: فَأَطْلَقَ ٱلْأَمِيرُ ٱلشَّابَّ مُوصِيًا إِيَّاهُ أَنْ: «لَا تَقُلْ لِأَحَدٍ إِنَّكَ أَعْلَمْتَنِي بِهَذَا».
verses.kjv: So the chief captain [then] let the young man depart, and charged [him, See thou] tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.web: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”

verses.ar: ثُمَّ دَعَا ٱثْنَيْنِ مِنْ قُوَّادِ ٱلْمِئَاتِ وَقَالَ: «أَعِدَّا مِئَتَيْ عَسْكَرِيٍّ لِيَذْهَبُوا إِلَى قَيْصَرِيَّةَ، وَسَبْعِينَ فَارِسًا وَمِئَتَيْ رَامِحٍ، مِنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ ٱلثَّالِثَةِ مِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ.
verses.kjv: And he called unto [him] two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
verses.web: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”

verses.ar: وَأَنْ يُقَدِّمَا دَوَابَّ لِيُرْكِبَا بُولُسَ وَيُوصِلَاهُ سَالِمًا إِلَى فِيلِكْسَ ٱلْوَالِي».
verses.kjv: And provide [them] beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring [him] safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.web: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

verses.ar: وَكَتَبَ رِسَالَةً حَاوِيَةً هَذِهِ ٱلصُّورَةَ:
verses.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
verses.web: He wrote a letter like this:

verses.ar: «كُلُودِيُوسُ لِيسِيَاسُ، يُهْدِي سَلَامًا إِلَى ٱلْعَزِيزِ فِيلِكْسَ ٱلْوَالِي:
verses.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix [sendeth] greeting.
verses.web: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

verses.ar: هَذَا ٱلرَّجُلُ لَمَّا أَمْسَكَهُ ٱلْيَهُودُ وَكَانُوا مُزْمِعِينَ أَنْ يَقْتُلُوهُ، أَقْبَلْتُ مَعَ ٱلْعَسْكَرِ وَأَنْقَذْتُهُ، إِذْ أُخْبِرْتُ أَنَّهُ رُومَانِيٌّ.
verses.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.web: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

verses.ar: وَكُنْتُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَعْلَمَ ٱلْعِلَّةَ ٱلَّتِي لِأَجْلِهَا كَانُوا يَشْتَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَنْزَلْتُهُ إِلَى مَجْمَعِهِمْ،
verses.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
verses.web: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

verses.ar: فَوَجَدْتُهُ مَشْكُوًّا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ جِهَةِ مَسَائِلِ نَامُوسِهِمْ. وَلَكِنَّ شَكْوَى تَسْتَحِقُّ ٱلْمَوْتَ أَوِ ٱلْقُيُودَ لَمْ تَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ.
verses.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.web: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

verses.ar: ثُمَّ لَمَّا أُعْلِمْتُ بِمَكِيدَةٍ عَتِيدَةٍ أَنْ تَصِيرَ عَلَى ٱلرَّجُلِ مِنَ ٱلْيَهُودِ، أَرْسَلْتُهُ لِلْوَقْتِ إِلَيْكَ، آمِرًا ٱلْمُشْتَكِينَ أَيْضًا أَنْ يَقُولُوا لَدَيْكَ مَا عَلَيْهِ. كُنْ مُعَافًى».
verses.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what [they had] against him. Farewell.
verses.web: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”

verses.ar: فَٱلْعَسْكَرُ أَخَذُوا بُولُسَ كَمَا أُمِرُوا، وَذَهَبُوا بِهِ لَيْلًا إِلَى أَنْتِيبَاتْرِيسَ.
verses.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought [him] by night to Antipatris.
verses.web: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

verses.ar: وَفِي ٱلْغَدِ تَرَكُوا ٱلْفُرْسَانَ يَذْهَبُونَ مَعَهُ وَرَجَعُوا إِلَى ٱلْمُعَسْكَرِ.
verses.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.web: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

verses.ar: وَأُولَئِكَ لَمَّا دَخَلُوا قَيْصَرِيَّةَ وَدَفَعُوا ٱلرِّسَالَةَ إِلَى ٱلْوَالِي، أَحْضَرُوا بُولُسَ أَيْضًا إِلَيْهِ.
verses.kjv: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.web: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

verses.ar: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَ ٱلْوَالِي ٱلرِّسَالَةَ، وَسَأَلَ مِنْ أَيَّةِ وِلَايَةٍ هُوَ، وَوَجَدَ أَنَّهُ مِنْ كِيلِيكِيَّةَ،
verses.kjv: And when the governor had read [the letter], he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that [he was] of Cilicia;
verses.web: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

verses.ar: قَالَ: «سَأَسْمَعُكَ مَتَى حَضَرَ ٱلْمُشْتَكُونَ عَلَيْكَ أَيْضًا». وَأَمَرَ أَنْ يُحْرَسَ فِي قَصْرِ هِيرُودُسَ.
verses.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
verses.web: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
